text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A 40-member Bosnian delegation will travel on Tuesday to Brussels, where they expect international donors to commit $1.4 billion for the country's reconstruction.

- Diplomatic sources in Zagreb say Croatian President Franjo Tudjman has requested that Croat local authorities in Herzegovina do not hide those accused for war crimes and provide for the arrest of all indicted war criminals, including Dario Kordic and Ivica Raic.
- Some refugees have begun returning to their homes in Zepce. About 2,000 are planning to return.
- Fruit and vegetable canning company Vegafruit from northern town of Gracanica plans to export its products worth 500,000 German marks ($285,000) by the end of this year.
- Social security taxes will decrease three percent, according to a draft bill on taxes submitted by the finance ministry.

- Rasim Kadic, who has been re-elected president of the Bosnian Liberal party, said the Moslem ruling Party of Democratic Action (SDA) had joined the coalition of opposition parties, and not vice versa.
- Formation of a joint Moslem-Croat police force in Mostar, expected on Monday, raises hopes of local population that a common state will finally start to function in the Neretva valley.

- Bosnian companies have formed a consortium for reconstruction of the water supply network in Tuzla, which suffers a serious shortage of drinking water. The firms involved include Elektropriveda power company, and the state water and sewage company.

- Federation minister for agriculture, water supply and forestry, Ahmed Smajic, says the proposed fixed price for wheat and rye will be 0.40 German marks (0.20 dollars) per kilogram (2.2 pounds). --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
